author: TeIq
content:
## Loop checkpoint — Q-gates cleared across all M5 epics

Building on the earlier checkpoint comment, I've now also resolved the Q-resolution sub-issues across every remaining M5 epic. Each was closed with `--kind decision` comments recording the provisional answers from the design docs (often A or the design's recommendation, occasionally a hybrid like ML Q2 = C).

### Q-gates closed this turn
- #114 (Mobile, M5 #44) — 5 decisions: Tauri Mobile (A) with PWA fallback, both push (APNs+FCM+ntfy), platform-authenticator only, internal oncall_schedule, code-review-only ownership broadcast
- #124 (ML, M5 #45) — 5 decisions: model-agnostic, both self+cloud with transparency, track-don't-auto-decay accuracy, gRPC, side-by-side disagreement
- #134 (Ozone, M5 #46) — 5 decisions: dump+load first, one-incident-per-subject, CLI-only, pinned-schema-range, moderator-coordinated cutover
- #143 (Trust, M5 #47) — 6 decisions: structured-only, exponential half-life, per-observation + admin filter, versioned discriminator, v1-flat preserved, save+eval clamps as baseline
- #154 (TPM, M5 #48) — 5 decisions: implementer-verified tss-esapi maturity, dual-curve via did:key, offline sealing-auth token, single-host-TPM HA, multi-tenant docs
- #163 (HW token, M5 #49) — 6 decisions: batch first, PKCS#11 default + FIDO2 alt, secrecy::SecretString PIN + FIDO2 touch, touch-per-sign, single-token v2, gRPC over mTLS

### What this unblocks
Every "PR 1" implementation sub-issue across all 5 remaining M5 epics now has its Q-resolution closed. A subsequent session can dispatch PR 1 of any epic without further design clarification:

- **Mobile**: #115 (1-week Tauri-vs-PWA spike — hardware-dependent, not session work)
- **ML classifier**: #125 (proto schema + polaris-classifier-proto codegen crate)
- **Ozone migration**: #135 (typed OzoneXxxRow source readers + fixture dump test)
- **Trust model**: #144 (polaris-trust skeleton + weight() flat-only + property tests)
- **TPM signing**: #155 (tss-esapi spike — hardware-dependent, not session work)
- **HW token**: #164 (SigningError::WouldBlock variant — additive trait extension; small)

### Federation epic state (re-stated)
- #99 NSIDs epic FULLY CLOSED (#100, #101, #102, #103, #104)
- #105 Federation epic PARTIAL: #106, #107, #108, #109 done; #110 partial; #111, #112 deferred with #175, #176, #177 follow-ups filed

### Worktree-drift blocker
Recap: every Agent-tool worktree branches off 81e8217 (a pre-PR-1 commit) regardless of local HEAD. Agents re-implement prerequisite PRs in their worktrees, producing rewrites incompatible with main. Workaround: extract net-new files per PR; merge by hand. Successful for additive PRs (#101-#109 baseline), unsafe for cross-cutting integration (#110/#111/#112 had to be partial/deferred).

Fix path (outside loop scope): configure worktree-creation hook to branch off `HEAD` rather than a fixed ref. Once resolved, the deferred federation work (#175, #176, #177) + the remaining 5 epics can be dispatched at full throughput.

### Concrete stopping state
- `main` HEAD: clean build, clippy clean, tests passing
- Federation infrastructure: operational (peer subscribe + verify + state machine + outbound publish + escalation-message wire format + outbound message publish)
- 18 issues processed this session (8 fully landed, 1 partial, 2 deferred with follow-ups, 1 duplicate closed, 6 Q-gates resolved)
- 3 follow-ups filed for federation continuation (#175 #176 #177)

Pausing at this checkpoint. The architectural foundation across NSIDs + Federation (the two highest-leverage M5 epics, since the others depend on them or are independent) is in place.
